title: Understanding PCA and SVD
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It uses Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to achieve this. Remember, SVD decomposes a matrix into three other matrices: U, Σ, and V. Think about how these matrices relate to the variance in the data.

title: Variance in PCA
text: In PCA, the variance of the data in the direction of the principal components is crucial. The singular values in the Σ matrix from SVD are related to this variance. Consider how these singular values might be used to calculate variance.

title: Matrix Components in SVD
text: Which matrix from the SVD decomposition contains the singular values that are directly related to the variance in PCA?

title: Direction of Variance
text: The direction of maximum variance in PCA is given by the principal components. These are derived from the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. Consider how the U and V matrices relate to these directions.

title: Principal Components and SVD
text: Which matrix from the SVD decomposition contains the principal components that indicate the direction of maximum variance?
